summary: Encoder scale variance + fallback to CPU shard causing rerank score skew and tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a mid-week deploy they started seeing re-ranked results that diverge from expected relevance and a 95th percentile latency spike on rerank calls. The problem appears correlated with bulk ingestion jobs that compute embeddings and subsequent rerank requests. Impact:
- Relevance drift: top-5 results reordered for ~8% of queries compared to baseline, causing product UX regression for Cordelia Health dashboards.
- Latency: rerank p95 increased from ~180ms to ~1.6s during ingestion windows.
Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: cordelia-prod (dedicated pool, us-east).
- Reranker service pinned to reranker-bert-qa:v2026-03-04.
- Embedding jobs using embedder-sim-v2 via our embeddings API.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Run batch ingestion of ~12k documents using embeddings endpoint with client SDK default settings (no explicit normalization).
2) Immediately issue rerank requests against the freshly indexed items.
3) Observe rerank ordering vs baseline and measure p95 latency on rerank endpoint.
Logs / sample traces:
- Trace IDs: trace-20260310-8f1a, trace-20260310-8f2b.
- Rerank service logs show frequent fallback to variant "reranker-bert-qa-cpu-quant" for ~22% of requests during ingestion window.
- Example latency sample: 2026-03-10T14:23:12Z rerank request id=abc123 p95=1610ms, model_variant=cpu-quant, queue_wait=1200ms.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger large embedding bulk ingest (~10-15k docs) using client SDK default settings
Immediately run standard rerank queries against the new index
Compare top-K ordering with a known-good baseline and capture rerank p95
logs:
Rerank service log excerpt:
[2026-03-10T14:23:11Z] INFO rerank-handler request=abc123 routing=pool-dedicated decision=fallthrough_to_cpu_variant reason=capacity_threshold queue_wait_ms=1187
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] WARN reranker-bert-qa-cpu-quant score_distribution_shift=0.23 topk_mismatch=0.08
Embedding ingestion job:
[2026-03-10T14:20:05Z] INFO embed-job batch=ingest-987 compute_ms_per_doc=17 normalization_flag=off
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: embedding vectors generated during bulk ingest were not L2-normalized; downstream reranker index expects normalized vectors -> score scaling leads to reordered topk.

Observed that ~22% of rerank requests were routed to a CPU-quantized variant because the GPU pool hit autoscale/burst thresholds during ingest; CPU variant uses a slightly different input preprocessing pipeline which lacks server-side normalization (introduced in earlier opt-in change).
Correlated client SDK usage: Cordelia's ingestion pipeline used an older SDK (v0.9.2) which omitted the new 'normalize' parameter default introduced in v1.1.0.

Confirmed through sample vectors: mean L2 norm for vectors produced in ingest window = 3.8 (unnormalized) vs baseline = 1.0 (normalized). Cosine-based scores diverge when magnitude varies; retrieval index search combined raw dot-product scoring then normalized by precomputed lengths in some paths but not all, causing inconsistency.
comments: Asha Patel (Support): Received initial report from Cordelia customer success; asking for traces and sample ids.
Cordelia (Customer): Sending sample query and affected doc ids, attaching ingestion job id (ingest-987).
SRE (Marta Rivera): Noted autoscale events in prod-us-east at 14:18-14:30; several pods terminated/restarted due to memory pressure during ingest.
Engineers (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally by running batch ingest with client SDK v0.9.2; confirming unnormalized embeddings and rerank variant fallback to cpu-quant.
Support (Asha Patel): Temporary mitigation suggested: re-run embedding step with explicit 'normalize=true' or pin rerank route to GPU pool until ingestion completes.
resolution:
Workaround applied and permanent fix outlined:
Short term: Advised Cordelia to re-ingest affected batches using SDK v1.1.0 with explicit normalize=true. Support added a routing override for their tenant to prioritize GPU variants while they reprocessed data. This immediately resolved p95 latency back to ~210ms and restored top-k ordering to expected baseline.
Long term: Deployed hotfix to rerank service to perform server-side L2 normalization for incoming vectors when model variants differ in preprocessing (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/3210). Updated autoscaling policy to add headroom during large ingests.
Follow-ups: 1) Add telemetry metric for embedding L2 norm distribution per ingest job. 2) Update SDK and docs to highlight 'normalize' flag and bump default in next release. 3) Postmortem to be published and linked from support ticket.
Status: Resolved and verified with customer on 2026-03-12.
